# requireNonException

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not an `Exception`.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonException() — Returns the value after checking that it is not an `Exception`. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonException<T>(
  value: T | Exception,
  message: string = "Expected a value that is not an Exception."
): T;
```

The library's own hierarchy only. A plain `Error` does not qualify, which is exactly what makes the check useful in a `catch` block that has to tell the two apart.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                               | Type             | Description                                                   |
| :---------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                                 | `T \| Exception` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a value that is not an Exception."` | `string`         | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T` — the same value, with an `Exception` excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                    |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is an `Exception`. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonException(new Error()); // => new Error()
requireNonException({}); // => {}
requireNonException(new IllegalArgumentException()); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
